```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Nakagawa 2026 gave eight FDA-approved antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) as a
single intravenous bolus to human FcRn transgenic Tg32 mice and to wild-type
C57BL/6J mice, measured **total ADC** (anti-payload capture assay) and **total
antibody** (anti-human IgG sandwich assay) in plasma for 28 days, and fitted a
two-compartment model to every animal in WinNonlin. The study's purpose is
translational: the Tg32 total-ADC clearance is then scaled to humans with a
single-species allometric exponent, and the optimal exponent (1.0) predicts
human clearance within twofold for seven of the eight ADCs.

None of the ADCs cross-reacts with its mouse target antigen, so every profile
is target-independent and linear. The authors fitted each ADC, strain and
analyte separately, so the paper contributes **32** independent model files,
one per combination, all sharing the same two-compartment structure:

```{r models}
drugs <- c(
  "tisotumabVedotin", "loncastuximabTesirine", "sacituzumabGovitecan",
  "trastuzumabDeruxtecan", "polatuzumabVedotin", "inotuzumabOzogamicin",
  "trastuzumabEmtansine", "datopotamabDeruxtecan"
)
drug_labels <- c(
  tisotumabVedotin = "Tisotumab vedotin",
  loncastuximabTesirine = "Loncastuximab tesirine",
  sacituzumabGovitecan = "Sacituzumab govitecan",
  trastuzumabDeruxtecan = "Trastuzumab deruxtecan",
  polatuzumabVedotin = "Polatuzumab vedotin",
  inotuzumabOzogamicin = "Inotuzumab ozogamicin",
  trastuzumabEmtansine = "Trastuzumab emtansine",
  datopotamabDeruxtecan = "Datopotamab deruxtecan"
)
grid <- expand.grid(
  analyte = c("adc", "tab"),
  strain = c("tg32mouse", "wtmouse"),
  drug = drugs,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
grid$model <- sprintf("Nakagawa_2026_%s_%s_%s", grid$drug, grid$strain, grid$analyte)
# Single IV bolus: 1 mg/kg (1000 ug/kg), except inotuzumab ozogamicin at 0.1 mg/kg.
grid$dose_ugkg <- ifelse(grid$drug == "inotuzumabOzogamicin", 100, 1000)

# Parse every model and collect its typical values (all 32 share one model()).
uis <- lapply(grid$model, function(m) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(m)))
names(uis) <- grid$model
theta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(uis, function(u) {
  th <- u$theta
  data.frame(
    cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]), vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]),
    q = exp(th[["lq"]]), vp = exp(th[["lvp"]])
  )
}))
grid <- cbind(grid, theta)
nrow(grid)
```

* Citation: `r uis[[1]]$reference`
* Article: [Clin Transl Sci 2026;19:e70692](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70692)

Example description (Tg32 total ADC, trastuzumab deruxtecan):

```{r description, echo = FALSE}
cat(strwrap(uis[["Nakagawa_2026_trastuzumabDeruxtecan_tg32mouse_adc"]]$description, 76), sep = "\n")
```

# Population

Male human FcRn transgenic Tg32 mice (B6.Cg-Fcgrt Tg(FCGRT)32Dcr/DcrJ, 5 weeks
old at purchase) and male wild-type C57BL/6J mice (5 or 6 weeks old), both from
The Jackson Laboratory Japan, n = 3 per ADC and strain (Methods,
Pharmacokinetic Study). Each mouse received one tail-vein bolus of 1 mg/kg in
10 mL/kg, except inotuzumab ozogamicin at 0.1 mg/kg. Blood was taken from the
jugular vein at 5 min, 4 h, 7 h and 1, 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days. Body weights
were not reported; the allometric scaling assumed 20 g for every mouse. The
ADC panel (Table 2) spans five payloads (MMAE, PBD, SN-38, DXd, calicheamicin,
DM1), drug-to-antibody ratios from 2.3 to 7.8, and one non-cleavable linker
(trastuzumab emtansine).

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Nakagawa_2026_trastuzumabDeruxtecan_tg32mouse_adc")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every model has the same `model()` block: a linear two-compartment model with
`kel = cl/vc`, `k12 = q/vc`, `k21 = q/vp`, IV bolus into `central`, and
`Cc = central/vc`. Parameters are normalised to body weight (mL/kg, mL/day/kg),
so the dose is entered in ug/kg and `Cc` is in ug/mL, the units of Figures 1
and 2. The values below are read back from the 32 packaged model files; each
file's in-line comments give the table cell and the mean +/- SD (n = 3).

| Quantity | Source location |
|----------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment structure | Methods (Pharmacokinetic Analysis); Results, "Comparative Analysis Between Mice and Human" |
| `lcl` (CL, mL/day/kg) | Table 3, total ADC and total antibody columns for Tg32 and WT |
| `lvc` (Vc, mL/kg) | Supplement Table S3 |
| `lq` (Q, mL/day/kg) | Supplement Table S4 |
| `lvp` (Vp, mL/kg) | Supplement Table S5 |
| `propSd` | not reported (individual WinNonlin fits); held at 0 |
| Dose 1 mg/kg (0.1 mg/kg inotuzumab ozogamicin) | Methods, Pharmacokinetic Study |

```{r param-table}
grid |>
  mutate(Drug = drug_labels[drug]) |>
  select(Drug, strain, analyte, cl, vc, q, vp) |>
  arrange(strain, analyte) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Strain = strain, Analyte = analyte, "CL (mL/day/kg)" = cl,
    "Vc (mL/kg)" = vc, "Q (mL/day/kg)" = q, "Vp (mL/kg)" = vp
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Simulation

The paper reports no between-animal variability or residual-error model, so
each model is solved at its typical values. Because the 32 files share one
`model()` block, the solve below compiles the first model once and supplies
the other 31 parameter sets as per-subject parameters (one subject per model).

```{r simulate}
sample_times <- c(5 / 1440, 4 / 24, 7 / 24, 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28)
fine_times <- seq(0, 28, by = 0.1)
grid$id <- seq_len(nrow(grid))

ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = grid$dose_ugkg[i], evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(
      id = i, time = sort(unique(c(0, sample_times, fine_times))),
      amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central"
    )
  )
}))
params <- grid |>
  transmute(id, lcl = log(cl), lvc = log(vc), lq = log(q), lvp = log(vp))

# rxode2 warns whenever several subjects are solved without an omega matrix;
# here each subject is a different model by design, so that warning is muffled.
sim <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    uis[[1]], events = ev, params = params,
    returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
  ),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
) |>
  left_join(select(grid, id, drug, strain, analyte, model), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    Drug = factor(drug_labels[drug], levels = drug_labels),
    Analyte = ifelse(analyte == "adc", "Total ADC", "Total antibody")
  )
```

## Figures 1 and 2: plasma concentration-time profiles

Replicates Figure 1 (Tg32) and Figure 2 (wild-type) of Nakagawa 2026: typical
profiles of total ADC and total antibody after a single IV bolus. The points
mark the paper's sampling times.

```{r fig1, fig.height = 5}
plot_strain <- function(st, title) {
  # Figures 1 and 2 use a 0.001-1000 ug/mL axis; inotuzumab ozogamicin total
  # ADC falls below its floor late in the profile.
  d <- dplyr::filter(sim, strain == st, Cc >= 0.001)
  ggplot(d, aes(time, Cc, linetype = Analyte, colour = Analyte)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(data = dplyr::filter(d, time %in% sample_times), size = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~Drug, nrow = 2) +
    scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.001, 1000)) +
    labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/mL)", title = title) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
plot_strain("tg32mouse", "Tg32 mice (replicates Figure 1)")
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 5}
plot_strain("wtmouse", "Wild-type C57BL/6J mice (replicates Figure 2)")
```

# PKNCA validation against Tables S1 and S2

The paper's NCA (Supplement Tables S1 and S2) is the mean of three individual
analyses on the sampling schedule above. The simulated profiles are passed to
PKNCA on the same schedule plus the time-zero bolus concentration.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, sample_times), !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, model, drug, strain, analyte, time, Cc)
dose <- grid |>
  transmute(id, model, drug, strain, analyte, time = 0, amt = dose_ugkg)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | strain + analyte + drug + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose, amt ~ time | strain + analyte + drug + id,
  route = "intravascular"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE, vss.obs = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca, ref,
  by = c("strain", "analyte", "drug"),
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cl.obs", "vss.obs"),
  units = c(
    cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "ug*day/mL", half.life = "day",
    cl.obs = "mL/day/kg", vss.obs = "mL/kg"
  )
)
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 1)
```

`r attr(cmp, "footnote")`

```{r nca-assert}
pct <- abs(as.numeric(sub("%.*$", "", cmp[["% diff"]])))
by_param <- split(pct, cmp[["NCA parameter"]])
stats_by_param <- vapply(
  by_param,
  function(x) c(median = median(x), p90 = unname(quantile(x, 0.9)), max = max(x)),
  numeric(3)
)
round(stats_by_param, 1)
# The half-life row is the only label starting with "t".
is_half <- startsWith(colnames(stats_by_param), "t")
stopifnot(
  ncol(stats_by_param) == 5, sum(is_half) == 1,
  # Exposure (AUC, CL, Vss) and the 5-min peak are set directly by the
  # transcribed CL, Vc and Vp: a mis-transcribed cell moves them by tens of
  # percent.
  all(stats_by_param["median", !is_half] < 5),
  all(stats_by_param["p90", !is_half] < 15),
  # The terminal half-life depends on which samples each analysis selects.
  stats_by_param["median", is_half] < 10
)
```

The typical-value profiles reproduce the paper's NCA closely. The largest
differences belong to wild-type polatuzumab vedotin, whose individual CL, Q and
Vp estimates vary by 60 to 70 percent between the three mice (Table 3, Tables
S4 and S5): the NCA of the mean animal and the mean of three NCAs then differ
by Jensen's inequality, not because of a transcription error. Terminal
half-lives differ most where the paper's 28-day schedule leaves few
terminal-phase samples (total antibody of loncastuximab tesirine and
trastuzumab deruxtecan in Tg32 mice).

# Allometric scaling to humans

The paper scales mouse parameters with
`P_human = P_mouse x (BW_human / BW_mouse)^e`, with `BW_mouse` = 20 g and the
human body weight taken from each clinical population-PK report (Table 1). Per
kilogram this is `P_human/kg = P_mouse/kg x (BW_human / 0.02)^(e - 1)`. The
human body weight is not printed, but it follows exactly from Table 1 (human CL
in L/day or L/h) and Table 4 (the same CL in mL/day/kg).

```{r allometry}
human <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~cl_h, ~cl_unit, ~vc_h, ~q_h, ~q_unit, ~vp_h, ~cl_h_perkg,
  "tisotumabVedotin", 1.42, "L/day", 3.1, 4.01, "L/day", 4.47, 18.9,
  "loncastuximabTesirine", 0.2621, "L/day", 3.86, 1.16, "L/day", 3.53, 3.36,
  "sacituzumabGovitecan", 0.133, "L/h", 2.77, 0.006, "L/h", 0.908, 45.6,
  "trastuzumabDeruxtecan", 0.421, "L/day", 2.77, 0.199, "L/day", 5.16, 7.28,
  "polatuzumabVedotin", 0.0344, "L/h", 3.15, 0.0145, "L/h", 3.98, 11.0,
  "inotuzumabOzogamicin", 0.113, "L/h", 6.7, 0.0405, "L/h", 5.1, 37.0,
  "trastuzumabEmtansine", 0.676, "L/day", 3.127, 1.534, "L/day", 0.66, 9.66,
  "datopotamabDeruxtecan", 0.416, "L/day", 3.02, 0.341, "L/day", 2.84, 6.48
) |>
  mutate(
    to_ml_day = ifelse(cl_unit == "L/h", 24000, 1000),
    bw_h = cl_h * to_ml_day / cl_h_perkg
  )
round(setNames(human$bw_h, drug_labels[human$drug]), 1)

tg32_adc <- grid |>
  dplyr::filter(strain == "tg32mouse", analyte == "adc") |>
  left_join(human, by = "drug")
scale_perkg <- function(p, bw, e) p * (bw / 0.02)^(e - 1)
# Prediction error as defined in the paper: relative to the observed value for
# an overprediction and to the predicted value for an underprediction.
pred_err <- function(pred, obs) ifelse(pred >= obs, (pred - obs) / obs, (pred - obs) / pred) * 100
```

## Table 4: human CL of total ADC from Tg32 mice

```{r table4}
exps <- c(0.85, 0.9, 0.95, 1, 1.05, 1.1)
table4_paper <- rbind(
  c(3.45, 5.21, 7.86, 11.9, 17.9, 27.0),
  c(2.67, 4.04, 6.10, 9.23, 13.9, 21.1),
  c(8.42, 12.7, 19.0, 28.6, 43.0, 64.7),
  c(2.58, 3.85, 5.74, 8.54, 12.7, 19.0),
  c(4.34, 6.55, 9.88, 14.9, 22.5, 33.9),
  c(7.95, 12.0, 18.1, 27.2, 41.0, 61.9),
  c(2.47, 3.71, 5.58, 8.39, 12.6, 19.0),
  c(3.83, 5.73, 8.58, 12.8, 19.2, 28.8)
)
pred4 <- outer(seq_len(8), exps, function(i, e) scale_perkg(tg32_adc$cl[i], tg32_adc$bw_h[i], e))
dimnames(pred4) <- list(drug_labels[tg32_adc$drug], paste0("e = ", exps))
knitr::kable(pred4, digits = 2)

pe4 <- apply(pred4, 2, pred_err, obs = tg32_adc$cl_h_perkg)
summary4 <- data.frame(
  exponent = exps,
  within_2fold = colMeans(abs(pe4) <= 100) * 100,
  within_3fold = colMeans(abs(pe4) <= 200) * 100,
  rmse = sqrt(colMeans(sweep(pred4, 1, tg32_adc$cl_h_perkg)^2))
)
summary4 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Exponent = exponent, "Within 2-fold (%)" = within_2fold,
    "Within 3-fold (%)" = within_3fold, "RMSE (mL/day/kg)" = rmse
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  # Every cell of Table 4 is reproduced from the packaged CL (Table 3 rounds to
  # one decimal, so the e = 1 column differs from the paper by that rounding).
  max(abs(pred4 / table4_paper - 1)) < 0.02,
  # Paper: optimal exponent 1.0, 87.5% within twofold, RMSE 8.12.
  summary4$within_2fold[summary4$exponent == 1] == 87.5,
  abs(summary4$rmse[summary4$exponent == 1] - 8.12) < 0.1,
  # Only loncastuximab tesirine falls outside twofold (2.75-fold over).
  identical(names(which(abs(pe4[, "e = 1"]) > 100)), "Loncastuximab tesirine")
)
```

The paper's summary rows (Table 4) are 25.0, 50.0, 62.5, 87.5, 62.5 and 50.0%
within twofold and RMSE 18.00, 15.68, 12.34, 8.12, 7.66 and 18.07 for exponents
0.85 to 1.1; the table above recomputes them from the model parameters.

## Figure 3: correlation of total-ADC CL between mice and humans

```{r fig3, fig.height = 4}
fig3 <- grid |>
  dplyr::filter(analyte == "adc") |>
  left_join(select(human, drug, cl_h_perkg), by = "drug") |>
  mutate(Strain = ifelse(strain == "tg32mouse", "Tg32", "Wild type"))
r2 <- fig3 |>
  group_by(Strain) |>
  summarise(r2 = cor(cl, cl_h_perkg)^2)
knitr::kable(dplyr::rename(r2, "R-squared" = r2), digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(r2$r2[r2$Strain == "Tg32"] - 0.888) < 0.005,
  abs(r2$r2[r2$Strain == "Wild type"] - 0.308) < 0.005
)
ggplot(fig3, aes(cl, cl_h_perkg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~Strain, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Mouse total ADC CL (mL/day/kg)", y = "Human CL (mL/day/kg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Nakagawa 2026: R-squared 0.888 for Tg32 and 0.308 for
wild-type mice.

## Projected human two-compartment parameters

The paper also titrated exponents for Vc, Q and Vp (Supplement Tables S6 to
S8) and reports the values that maximise the twofold accuracy as 1.05 for Vc,
0.65 to 0.8 for Q and 0.95 for Vp; it notes that these parameters did not
correlate significantly between mice and humans (Figure S1) and that their use
for clinical profile prediction needs further work. The table below applies
those exponents (both ends of the Q range) to the Tg32 total-ADC models and
sets the result against the human population-PK values of Table 1. It is
descriptive: no human model is packaged.

```{r human-projection}
proj <- tg32_adc |>
  transmute(
    Drug = drug_labels[drug],
    "BW (kg)" = bw_h,
    "CL pred / obs" = scale_perkg(cl, bw_h, 1) * bw_h / 1000 / (cl_h * to_ml_day / 1000),
    "Vc pred / obs" = scale_perkg(vc, bw_h, 1.05) * bw_h / 1000 / vc_h,
    "Q pred / obs (e = 0.65)" = scale_perkg(q, bw_h, 0.65) * bw_h / (q_h * to_ml_day),
    "Q pred / obs (e = 0.8)" = scale_perkg(q, bw_h, 0.8) * bw_h / (q_h * to_ml_day),
    "Vp pred / obs" = scale_perkg(vp, bw_h, 0.95) * bw_h / 1000 / vp_h
  )
knitr::kable(proj, digits = 2)
```

The human population-PK models behind Table 1 that are also in this library
are `Gibiansky_2022_tisotumab`, `Sathe_2024_sacituzumab`,
`Yin_2021_trastuzumabDeruxtecan`, `Lu_2019_polatuzumab`,
`Garrett_2019_inotuzumab` and `Lu_2014_trastuzumabemtansine`.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mean of individual fits.** The paper fitted each mouse separately in
  WinNonlin and reports the mean +/- SD of the three estimates; there is no
  population model. The packaged values are those means, with no
  between-animal variability (the SD of three individual estimates is not an
  estimate of omega) and the residual error held at zero.
* **One file per ADC, strain and analyte.** Total ADC and total antibody were
  fitted independently (for sacituzumab govitecan in Tg32 mice the total-ADC
  CL is even lower than the total-antibody CL), so they are separate models
  rather than one coupled deconjugation model. To simulate both analytes for
  one ADC, dose each model separately.
* **Per-kilogram units.** Parameters are kept in the paper's body-weight
  normalised units (mL/kg and mL/day/kg); dose in ug/kg (1 mg/kg = 1000 ug/kg)
  gives `Cc` in ug/mL. No body-weight covariate is carried, because the paper
  did not estimate one; the allometric scaling above is a separate,
  across-species translation step.
* **Table 4 rounding.** Table 4's exponent-1.0 column prints the Tg32 CL to
  three significant figures (9.23, 8.54, 8.39) where Table 3 prints one decimal
  (9.2, 8.5, 8.4); the packaged models use Table 3.
* **No human model.** The optimal Q exponent is reported only as a range (0.65
  to 0.8), and the paper presents the Vc, Q and Vp exponents as exploratory, so
  the human projection is shown above for reference only.
* **Errata.** No correction to the article was found in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-16).
